title: Houthi Drone Strike Hits Saudi Aramco's Jazan Refinery — Aramco Says 'No Material Operational or Financial Impact' as Oil Risk Premium Builds
detail: Iran-backed Houthi forces launched a coordinated drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery near the Saudi-Yemen border early Sunday, sparking a fire that was extinguished by authorities with no casualties reported at the facility (a separate Houthi strike on Yemen's al-Makha port killed seven people). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group targeted the refinery in retaliation for Saudi airspace violations. Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser acknowledged 'some production interruptions' from the recent wave of attacks but said operations would resume quickly and the strikes had 'no material operational or financial impact.' The attack — coming as the Strait of Hormuz corridor remains under strain from the broader US-Israel-Iran conflict — added a fresh, if contained, jolt to Gulf energy-supply risk just as markets were digesting the prior week's data, keeping oil's geopolitical risk premium elevated heading into the week's Treasury and inflation moves.
